criterion.ownedTruth: A busy non-technical leader can understand what is known, what matters and what to answer next.
passConditions: Each result can be understood by a bright 12-year-old without product or consulting jargon.
The language is concise enough to sequence into a simple interface with deeper detail available on demand.
There is one clear question, not several disguised asks.
Labels and boundaries clarify meaning rather than adding verbal clutter.
failConditions: The output is pompous, cryptic, abstract, e-learning-like or full of accessory text.
A leader must decode phrases before they can answer the question.
Several ideas or asks compete for attention.

hardVetoRules.condition: The main decision or question is unintelligible without specialist interpretation.

shared.label: Human agency
shared.rule: Humans own purpose, boundaries, standards, exceptions and the final consequential call.

shared.label: Evidence standing
shared.rule: Keep explicit facts, inferred candidates and behavioural feedback as different data types.

shared.label: Subject and audience boundary
shared.rule: Prove subject, ownership, audience and authority before an item can travel or act.

shared.label: Behavioural reality
shared.rule: Judge the real task and consequence, not an elegant description of the intended system.

optional.label: Recognition-first intake
optional.rule: Interpret the evidence first, then ask one concrete question only when its answer can change the route.
